kicker: Many paths lead into the mist — no one has reached the end.
summary: No one knows AI's future for sure — but we can choose where we stand.

quiz.q: One person says “AGI arrives in 2027”, another says “it's still far off”. What should you ask first?
options: What does each of them mean by AGI?
quiz.explain: Each side may use a different ruler: economic work, cognitive tests, or a panel's signature. Same word AGI, different definitions.

defs.label: Everyone has a definition
defs.art: Four engraved stones stand around a well full of mist. Each casts a different moon into it: a coin, a staircase, a ten-spoked wheel, a panel's seal. Touch a stone and one layer of mist clears.

view.text: AGI is a highly autonomous system that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. The ruler: work.
There is no single finish line: rank AI on a ladder by both skill and breadth, from “emerging” to “superhuman”.
AGI is AI as versatile and proficient as a well-educated adult, scored across 10 cognitive areas. They scored GPT-4 at 27% and GPT-5 at 57%.
When OpenAI declares AGI, an independent expert panel will verify it; many money terms between the two companies hinge on that day.

common.text: All four mean “broadly as capable as people”, but measure with different rulers: work, a ladder, tests, or a panel's signature.

insight.text: Arguments about “when AGI arrives” are often arguments about “what AGI is”. Ask for the definition before trusting a date.

tide.label: The rope that measures work
tide.art: A long scroll laid on silver sand. Drag the moon from left to right and the bamboo ropes measuring how long a task AI can do alone grow like tree shadows at moonset. The last mark sinks into the dawn mist and the rope's end fades away.

fact.text: METR measures how long a task (in human working hours) an AI can finish on its own. Claude 3.7 Sonnet reached about 1 hour; that length doubled roughly every 7 months for 6 years.
Google DeepMind's Gemini Deep Think solved 5 of 6 IMO problems, scoring 35/42, gold-medal level; IMO coordinators graded and confirmed it.
According to METR, an agent using GPT-5 finished tasks about 2 hours 17 minutes long, with a 50% success rate.
METR tested an early Claude Mythos Preview: at least 16 hours (confidence interval 8.5–55 hours). Beyond 16 hours, the current task suite can no longer measure reliably.
OpenAI announced that 10,000 agents found a “singularity” in the Navier–Stokes equations, checked in Lean; mathematicians are still reviewing it and no prize has been awarded.
METR's tracking page stopped updating on Sep 8, 2026; the latest model measured is Mythos Preview. The current ruler can't reliably measure beyond 16 hours.

horizon.text: If the trend holds, METR projects AI could handle month-long projects on its own before 2030.

insight.text: In about a year, the tasks AI can finish alone grew from about 1 hour to at least 16 hours, mostly in programming.

detail.text: Note: METR's tasks are mostly programming, machine learning and cybersecurity, self-contained and automatically graded. Real-world work is far messier.

fork.label: Three paths into the mist
fork.art: A fork in the stone path, sunk in mist at moonset. Three bamboo well-sweeps stand beside it. Pull one and the garden at the end of the path changes: a tangled wilderness, evenly shared terraces, an open common garden, or a high-walled garden only a few may enter.

note.text: This is a thinking tool built by AI Zen, not a forecast.

scenarios.name: Wilderness
scenarios.text: Fast progress, loose fences: many inventions, but accidents and misuse spread like weeds too.

scenarios.name: Common garden
scenarios.text: Fast, widely shared, well fenced: what many hope for, but it needs rare cooperation between countries and companies.

scenarios.name: Walled garden
scenarios.text: Tight control, but benefits pile up in a few places: safer, while the gap between rich and poor widens.

scenarios.name: Terraces
scenarios.text: Slow progress; society adapts step by step. Close to the “AI as normal technology” view.

scenarios.name: A path through the mist
scenarios.text: Everything in between: some benefits, some risks, and the outcome depends on each year's choices.

view.text: Scenario: AI speeds up AI research itself and by late 2027 beats experts at most tasks; it has two endings, “race” and “slowdown”.

mists.who: The AI 2027 team itself · note, Nov 2025

view.text: The authors say 2027 is only the “most likely single year”; their median forecasts are later, with one author at 2030.
AI will seep in over decades like earlier big technologies; people keep control if they build enough resilience.

insight.text: Scenarios are tools for thinking, not prophecies. People set these three levers; they don't move on their own.

trays.label: Three trays of work
trays.art: Three stone trays on a wooden veranda at moonset: one of white pebbles, dry and bright; one half under water; one still under thick mist. Pebbles engraved with tasks wait in a rattan basket for you to place them.
trays.keys: Pick a pebble, then press 1, 2 or 3 to place it in a tray
trays.match: You and the expert view agree on {n}/{total} pebbles

tasks.label: Write 20 headline options
tasks.why: Drafting many options is quick for AI; you still do the choosing.

tasks.label: Summarise 200 customer comments
tasks.why: Reading a lot and grouping ideas is a strength; spot-check a few original quotes.

tasks.label: Draft-translate a post into English
tasks.why: Good drafts; brand voice and wordplay still need a human edit.

tasks.label: Moodboard and concept images
tasks.why: Drafts are fast and cheap; images for real use need rights checks and a close look at details.

tasks.label: A finished, on-brand video ad
tasks.why: Single shots look great; keeping characters, product and pacing consistent is still hard.

tasks.label: Run a multi-week campaign alone
tasks.why: Agents handle longer chains of work every year, but hard-to-undo steps still need human sign-off.

tasks.label: Choose ideas that fit the brand's taste
tasks.why: Taste is an accountable choice, rooted in knowing customers and culture.

tasks.label: Keep relationships, own mistakes
tasks.why: Clients and partners need a person who stands behind the commitment.

expertNote.text: The “expert” sorting is AI Zen's editorial view as of Oct 2026, informed by METR and the WEF; it may change month to month.

insight.text: Skills worth investing in: taste, clear briefs, verification, directing AI, and human relationships.

detail.text: A survey of 1,000+ employers (WEF, Jan 2025) expects nearly 40% of core skills to change by 2030; creative thinking and tech skills matter more and more.

jobs.text: The same survey expects by 2030: 170 million new jobs, 92 million lost, a net gain of 78 million.
